evidence_items.locator: Prepared remarks, Oracle Q2 FY2026 call

receipt.public_excerpt: Cloud infrastructure revenue was $4.1 billion, up 66%, with GPU-related revenue growing 177%.

evidence_items.explanation: Oracle, which says most about GPUs, gave only a growth rate for GPU-related revenue, not a dollar figure. That fits the claim.

receipt.public_excerpt: Microsoft has never disclosed Azure’s quarterly revenue in dollars. It has typically only shared a growth percentage or described revenue dollar milestones in vague ways.

evidence_items.explanation: Before October 2026, including its January 2026 report (the last before the post), Microsoft did not give Azure revenue in dollars, let alone GPU rental revenue.

receipt.public_excerpt: our chips business, inclusive of Graviton and Trainium, is now over $10 billion in annual revenue run rate, growing triple-digit percentages year-over-year.

evidence_items.explanation: Amazon did put a number on its own-silicon business. But it is a run rate, not actual period revenue, and it combines Trainium with the Graviton CPU. It weakens the claim but does not contradict it on the plain reading.

unresolved_gaps: I found no source that directly documents Google's AI or GPU revenue disclosure practice in this period. Google Cloud is reported as one segment that includes Workspace.
Whether run-rate remarks count as disclosing revenue is a judgment call.
